html:
The Twenty Years' Anarchy is the name some historians give to the years 695 to 717 in the Byzantine Empire, when emperors were made and unmade by coups. It began when Justinian II was overthrown and mutilated, and ended when Leo III took the throne.

The rulers in order:

  • Leontios, 695 to 698, the general who overthrew Justinian
  • Tiberios III, 698 to 705, raised by the fleet after the loss of Carthage
  • Justinian II again, 705 to 711, back with Bulgar help
  • Philippikos, 711 to 713
  • Anastasios II, 713 to 715
  • Theodosios III, 715 to 717

While the army fought over the throne, the empire lost its last hold in North Africa when Carthage fell to the Umayyads in 698, and Arab armies pushed deep into Anatolia. The Bulgar ruler Tervel won land and a title for helping Justinian. Leo III came to power just in time to face the second Arab siege of Constantinople.
